correctness.rationale: For P=I/2+[[r,s],[s,-r]], the idempotent conic r^2+s^2=1/4 and trace orthogonality give P∘J={X=aI+[[u,v],[v,-u]]:ur+vs=a/2}. For Q=u²+v²≠0, line/conic solutions number 1+χ(Q−a²)=1+χ(−det X); Q=0 and scalars have separate, correctly handled cases. Standard nonzero-level character counts and zero-level split/aniso counts produce all four incidence fibers for each χ(−1)=±1, summing to q³. Any nontrivial terminal rank-one idempotent forces the Jordan word into P∘J, giving the one-sided excluded nonscalar counts; not a converse. Independently reconstructed every matrix/primitive-P incidence for q=3,5,7,11,13 with exact modular arithmetic and matched all displayed fibers. Field F_9 not independently rerun; general proof covers prime powers through quadratic characters.
residual_risks: Independent finite enumerations were for prime fields only; the unrestricted prime-power theorem is analytic, relying on standard finite-field character sums. No converse to Peirce-incidence necessity is established.
